items.title: John Budd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [transcript only]
items.q: And at that time I had read Horatio Alger stories — you ever heard of him?

ctx.x: My math isn’t quite up to snuff. And when you were a young man, what kind of music was the music of the day?

I had classical music piano lessons. I went to a neighbor who was a piano teacher and subsequent teachers and just learned to play music, and then finally went to the Conservatory in Halifax. They had young ladies mostly who were studying and you would employ one of them to teach you at good rates I guess, and you’d have one for a year and then she would go on to the next grade and I’d get another one. But I got the same thing again. So I learned how to read, how to put fingering into exercises, and how to…

that and said I think it is, I’ve had enough. So we quit. I took two years, I went to high school and in a couple of years there was a show put on and they had some people to play music, and there was not a piano player maybe. They got me to play and I began to play, and learned tunes like that. The birds are singing/I’ll feather your nest and songs like that. And all these old, old songs that day.
